group.passage: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), tooth decay that is left untreated is the most common health condition in the world, and diseases of the mouth affect about 3.7 billion people. Yet tooth decay does not happen overnight. It is the result of a daily battle inside your mouth, and understanding how this battle works can help you win it. The battle starts with plaque, a sticky film that forms on your teeth. Plaque is full of tiny bacteria, and these bacteria feed on the sugar in what you eat and drink. As they feed, they produce acid. This acid attacks enamel, the hard outer layer of a tooth, and pulls minerals out of it. Every time you eat a sweet snack, the bacteria get another chance to make acid. Luckily, your teeth can fight back. Saliva contains minerals that help enamel repair itself. In fact, teeth lose minerals and get them back many times a day. Problems begin when the losses are greater than the repairs. The first sign of trouble is a white spot on a tooth. At this stage, the damage can still be stopped or even reversed. If the acid attacks continue, however, so much of the hard outer layer is lost that a hole called a cavity forms. A cavity is permanent, and a dentist usually has to fill it. This is where fluoride comes in. Fluoride, which is found in toothpaste and in some tap water, helps enamel repair itself and makes it harder for acid to break down. It also makes it more difficult for bacteria to produce acid. For these reasons, the WHO recommends brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste. It also suggests eating less free sugar, which includes not only the sugar added to food but also the sugar in honey and fruit juice.

questions.stem: What is the passage mainly about?

options.A: How tooth decay develops and how it can be prevented.
options.B: Why the WHO keeps track of health problems around the world.
options.C: How dentists fill the holes in people’s teeth.
options.D: Why fruit juice is better for teeth than snacks.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what does the acid made by bacteria do to teeth?

options.A: It helps saliva repair the enamel.
options.B: It gives the bacteria sugar to feed on.
options.C: It takes minerals away from the enamel.
options.D: It forms a sticky film on the teeth.

questions.stem: In the first paragraph, what does “does not happen overnight” mean?

options.D: Can be cured in one day.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT mentioned as a way fluoride protects teeth?

options.C: It reduces the acid bacteria make.
options.D: It kills the bacteria in plaque.

1.explanation_zh: 第一段說蛀牙是口腔裡每天上演的一場「戰鬥」的結果，了解它就能打贏；第二段說細菌把糖變成酸、酸破壞琺瑯質；第三段說牙齒會自我修復，失去的比補回的多就會形成蛀洞；第四段說氟化物的幫助和世界衛生組織的建議。全文講的是蛀牙怎麼形成、怎麼預防。
evidence: It is the result of a daily battle inside your mouth, and understanding how this battle works can help you win it.
This is where fluoride comes in.

option_notes_zh.B: 世界衛生組織只是第一段數字的出處和最後的建議者，文章沒有談它如何追蹤全球的健康問題。
option_notes_zh.C: 牙醫補牙只在第三段最後一句提到，是局部細節。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中說「自由糖」也包括果汁裡的糖，並沒有說果汁比點心對牙齒好。

1.strategy_zh: 主旨題看第一段最後一句：作者要說明這場「戰鬥」怎麼進行、怎麼打贏，也就是蛀牙的成因與預防。
hints: 第一段最後一句說了解什麼可以幫你「打贏」？
第二、三段講蛀牙的什麼？第四段講什麼？
選同時包含「怎麼形成」和「怎麼預防」的選項。

2.explanation_zh: 第二段說細菌吃糖時會產生酸，這種酸會攻擊琺瑯質（牙齒堅硬的外層），把裡面的礦物質拉出來。也就是酸會帶走琺瑯質的礦物質。
evidence: This acid attacks enamel, the hard outer layer of a tooth, and pulls minerals out of it.

option_notes_zh.A: 幫助琺瑯質修復的是唾液裡的礦物質和氟化物，酸的作用正好相反。
option_notes_zh.B: 文中說細菌吃的是食物和飲料裡的糖，酸是細菌吃糖之後產生的，因果顛倒了。
option_notes_zh.D: 原文確實有 a sticky film that forms on your teeth，但那是在說明牙菌斑（plaque），不是酸的作用。

2.strategy_zh: 先找題幹的關鍵字 acid，看 This acid 那一句的動詞（attacks、pulls ... out）；選項若描述的是別的東西（牙菌斑、唾液），就要排除。
hints: 這種酸攻擊牙齒的哪一部分？把什麼拉出來？
sticky film 說的是酸，還是牙菌斑？

3.explanation_zh: 下一句接著說：蛀牙是口腔裡「每天」一場戰鬥的結果。可見 does not happen overnight 是「不是一夜之間發生的，需要一段時間慢慢形成」。
evidence: Yet tooth decay does not happen overnight.
It is the result of a daily battle inside your mouth, and understanding how this battle works can help you win it.

option_notes_zh.A: 把 overnight 當成「晚上睡覺時」的字面意思；文中完全沒提到睡覺。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中沒有說蛀牙只影響成人；這個片語說的是蛀牙形成的速度，不是哪些人會蛀牙。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中說蛀洞是永久的、要牙醫補，並沒有說一天就能治好。

3.strategy_zh: 片語題要看下一句的補充：a daily battle（每天的戰鬥）說明蛀牙是長期累積的。
hints: 找到第一段粗體的片語。
下一句說蛀牙是什麼的結果？
「每天的戰鬥」累積出來的結果，是快還是慢？

4.explanation_zh: 第四段說氟化物能幫助琺瑯質修復（A）、讓酸比較難破壞琺瑯質（B），也讓細菌比較難產生酸（C）。文中沒有說氟化物會殺死牙菌斑裡的細菌，所以答案是 D。
evidence: Fluoride, which is found in toothpaste and in some tap water, helps enamel repair itself and makes it harder for acid to break down.
It also makes it more difficult for bacteria to produce acid.

option_notes_zh.A: 文中有提到：氟化物 helps enamel repair itself。
option_notes_zh.B: 文中有提到：氟化物 makes it harder for acid to break down。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中有提到：氟化物讓細菌比較難產生酸（makes it more difficult for bacteria to produce acid）。

4.strategy_zh: NOT 題要逐一核對：把第四段關於 fluoride 的句子列成清單，文中有的選項刪掉，剩下的就是答案。注意「讓細菌少產生酸」和「殺死細菌」不一樣。
hints: 第四段說氟化物對琺瑯質有哪兩個幫助？
下一句說氟化物對細菌有什麼影響？
文中有沒有說氟化物會殺死細菌？

translation_zh.text:
根據世界衛生組織（WHO），沒有治療的蛀牙是全世界最常見的健康問題，而口腔疾病影響了大約 37 億人。然而，蛀牙並不是一夜之間形成的。它是你口腔裡每天上演的一場戰鬥的結果，了解這場戰鬥怎麼進行，就能幫助你打贏它。
這場戰鬥從牙菌斑開始，牙菌斑是一層在牙齒上形成的黏膩薄膜。牙菌斑裡滿是微小的細菌，這些細菌以你吃進、喝進的糖為食。它們一邊吃，一邊產生酸。這種酸會攻擊琺瑯質，也就是牙齒堅硬的外層，把裡面的礦物質拉出來。每當你吃一份甜食，細菌就又多了一次製造酸的機會。
幸好，你的牙齒會反擊。唾液含有礦物質，能幫助琺瑯質自我修復。事實上，牙齒一天之中會多次流失礦物質、再把它們補回來。當流失的比修復的多時，問題就開始了。最早的警訊是牙齒上的一個白點。在這個階段，損害還能被阻止，甚至恢復。然而，如果酸持續攻擊，堅硬的外層流失太多，就會形成一個叫做蛀洞的洞。蛀洞是永久的，通常必須由牙醫補起來。
這就是氟化物派上用場的地方。氟化物存在於牙膏和某些自來水中，它能幫助琺瑯質自我修復，並讓酸更難破壞琺瑯質。它也讓細菌更難產生酸。因為這些原因，世界衛生組織建議每天用含氟牙膏刷牙兩次。它也建議少吃自由糖，自由糖不只包括加進食物裡的糖，也包括蜂蜜和果汁裡的糖。
